To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EBV is associated with OSCCs and the LMP‐1 is expressed in neoplastic epithelial cells of EBV-positive OSCCs.
EBV was detected in 13 of 50 (26%) oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cases, and the latent membrane protein 1 (LMP-1) was expressed in 10 of 13 (77%) EBV-positive OSCC cases.
Epstein‐Barr Virus (EBV) was present in 10.5% (9/86) oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the expression of the LMP‐1 oncoprotein in EBV‐positive oral squamous cell carcinoma.

the study of Epstein‐Barr viral latent membrane protein‐2A (LMP2A) in the development of oral squamous cell carcinoma and the role of LMP2A in the regulation of epithelial‐mesenchymal transition (EMT).
the development of new and improved methods of cancer treatment and the identification and treatment of cancer in its earliest stages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EBV‐associated OSCC is a rare entity and the presence of EBVs in OSCC may be a consequence of the host's response to the tumor.
the presence of EBVs in the oral cavity is not associated with the development of OSCCs.
the presence of EBVs in OSCCs is not a frequent occurrence, and that the expression of EBV‐LMP‐1 in OSCCs is a rare event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EBV is present in OSCC and that LMP‐1 expression is associated with EBV‐positive tumors.
EBV‐LMP‐1 is not a major player in oral cancer.
EBV is associated with OSCCs in the Indian subcontinent and that LMP‐1 is expressed in neoplastic epithelial cells of EBV-positive OSCCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LMP‐1 expression in OSCCs is a marker of poor clinical outcomes, and that LMP‐1‐positive cells may be responsible for the poor clinical prognosis of OSCC patients.
LMP‐1 can be detected in the nuclei and cytoplasm of OSCC cell lines.
EBV is not only present in OSCCs, but also that the expression of Lmp1 is associated with a more aggressive phenotype of these tumors.
